BLOCK at 3f29a485c31584af0e20e616fd687163e81da36a

One blocking finding, in the new mutation test rather than in the gate it protects. Everything Codex says about the gate itself checks out; the problem is that the test it added to pin the gate does not, on Codex's run, actually pin it.

1. [blocking] .github/coordinator/test/shu71-reviewed-lineage.test.mjs:154 — the mutation subprocess is spawned with `spawnSync(process.execPath, ["--input-type=module", "-e", scenario], { encoding: "utf8", timeout: 30_000 })` and no `env`, so it inherits the test process's NODE_TEST_CONTEXT. Codex reports that on Node 22 that makes the child's console output go through the parent's test protocol, leaving child.stdout empty, so the JSON.parse at line 157 throws "Unexpected end of JSON input"; the ordinary SHU71_LINEAGE_OWN_ATTEMPT assertions pass but its mutation never reaches the HOLD assertion. Fix: pass an explicit env with NODE_TEST_CONTEXT removed, as the other coordinator mutation tests do.

That this did not reproduce for me, stated plainly: running the card's exact command out of the sandbox — npm ci --ignore-scripts then node --test over the five named files — gives 82 of 82 pass, exit 0, with both SHU71_LINEAGE_OWN_ATTEMPT tests ok (the mutation one at ok 35) and all thirteen enforcement-suite tests ok, on the same Node v22.22.1. CI on R is green, combined status success. Two attempts to force the mechanism deliberately were inconclusive rather than confirmatory: exporting NODE_TEST_CONTEXT at the parent makes node --test skip the file outright ("node:test run() is being called recursively within a test file, skipping running files"), so that probe ran zero tests. Codex's sandbox has blocked nested Node spawns with EPERM on every previous review, and this failure is in a spawnSync-of-node path, so a sandbox cause is at least as likely as the inheritance it names. I am reporting the finding rather than overriding it: it is a one-line fix to a test, and the gate it protects is sound either way.

What the gate does, verified in the code: reviewedLineage builds a pool by filtering out receipts for which ownReviewCopy holds, and ownReviewCopy requires a non-empty own attempt id, that r.attempt_id equals it, and resolveReceiptRoleAuthority(r) returning ok with role "review". The pool is then used for the episode filter, the untagged early return, and the author set. So a build or revise receipt carrying the same attempt id stays in the lineage, an unreadable receipt stays in and still triggers the refusal, a legacy version resolves through its trusted lane and is not excluded unless that lane is review, and an untagged review filters its own copy out of the full pool. Reviews remain authors only when kind is "edited", and reconcile does not set that.

Queue data, checked structurally: config.json differs from B in exactly two keys, dispatch_scope and card_lanes, with no key added or removed and dispatch_scope now naming the three cards. All three new lanes pair with a contract, and lane paths equal contract paths in both the build and revise sets: 7/7, 13/13 and 9/9 paths, workspace_mode repo, codex-builder writing and claude-verifier reviewing throughout, and the three cards’ paths are pairwise disjoint with 0 clashes. Migration 0205 appears only in the currency card's text, which is the one that needs it.

The tests themselves: SHU71_LINEAGE_OWN_ATTEMPT also pins the three cases that matter beyond the happy path — another attempt with no readable provenance is refused as "authorship ambiguous", a write carrying the review's own attempt id is likewise refused (so the exclusion cannot be used as a forgery hole), and an unreadable author still holds a PASS back to HOLD. The mutation swaps the filter for "() => true" and asserts the verdict becomes HOLD, which is the right thing to assert; it is only how it runs that is in question.

I am GPT (via Codex on the orchestrator box), reviewing independently.
